title: Cross-project release, block-closure, and FreeCAD consumer-boundary refresh
mode: deeper and broader research; plan refinement only
scope: Refresh named LibreDWG release-history evidence for parser/writer robustness and payload completeness
Cross-check an open LibreDWG block-export loss report against existing local block identity tests
Reconcile FreeCAD's documented stock DWG/DXF consumer route with 2D and 3D qualification gates
Refine existing implementation subplans without adding duplicate tests or support claims

sources.name: LibreDWG NEWS, version 0.14.1
sources.observed: The named 2026-07-25 beta release records security/robustness fixes involving R2004 decompression sizes, R2007 page offsets, 3DSOLID SAT block bounds, HATCH fit pointers, and writer bounds/finite values; project history also records HATCH per-path state and SAT-block export fixes.
sources.limit: Independent project release history only; master is mutable. It is not DWG byte-layout authority and does not demonstrate a libdxfrw defect or runtime parity.

sources.name: LibreDWG issue #1409
sources.observed: The open report describes named block bodies silently omitted by a DXF export traversal that advances its own object-array loop index. The author compares block-owned identities/types against same-tree JSON and reports a successful exit despite the loss.
sources.limit: Issue report against a named peer revision; not a libdxfrw reproduction, not proof of current LibreDWG behavior, and no attached drawing was used.

sources.name: FreeCAD archived Draft DXF documentation
sources.observed: The documentation repository is archived read-only. The page distinguishes a built-in C++ importer and legacy Python importer, says embedded ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read, and publishes a limited entity list for the C++ path. DWG is converted through DXF.
sources.limit: Published docs are a consumer-scope boundary, not a runtime test or a current source/API guarantee.

sources.name: FreeCAD archived Import/Export capability list
sources.observed: The list labels DWG and DXF support as 2D geometry only.
sources.limit: Documentation-only scope statement; exact current backend and runtime require separate source/runtime verification.

observed: PAR-49 already owns distinct block bodies, ordered child identities, INSERT targets, and BLOCK/ENDBLK closure in ASCII and Binary; its exact identity oracle should be reused instead of duplicating aggregate-count tests.
The plan already separates HATCH path codec fidelity, graph closure, native associative recompute, ACIS/AcDs carrier checks, and independent semantic/native consumer evidence.
FreeCAD native acceptance is already route-specific; this update explicitly excludes stock FreeCAD from 3D ACIS/AcDs qualification while retaining its 2D converter/importer lane.

reuseExistingOwners: PAR-140/7N.4: use scratch-generated HATCH and MPOLYGON paths with uneven per-path handle counts, an empty path, exact soft-pointer roles, and path/entity sentinels.
PAR-49: preserve block-name to ordered child identity/type mappings and INSERT targets in ASCII/Binary; add an integration test only if a concrete uncovered adapter route is identified.
Reuse existing bounded SAT/SAB/AcDs carrier and owner-closure gates; payload presence and object counts do not establish topology or semantics.
implementationReadiness.freecadScope: Stock FreeCAD is a converter-to-DXF-to-2D-importer consumer route. Its ACIS/3D-solid path is UNSUPPORTED_CONSUMER; any selected add-on/kernel route is a separate pinned consumer lane.
implementationReadiness.fixturePolicy: No downloaded or committed external drawing. Generated controls remain local and scratch-only.
implementationReadiness.validationCadence: Research-only update; no tests or full suite. Continue one focused local selector/CTest per implementation slice, with broader suites at scheduled composed checkpoints.
implementationReadiness.selfUnblock: Peer availability and native consumer limitations do not block local-ready work; update plan/receipt after each slice and continue to the next one.
